title: Exploited LiteLLM custom guardrail sandbox escape permits proxy code execution
summary: The custom-code guardrail endpoint allows bytecode techniques to escape its Python sandbox and execute code in the proxy process. CISA added this flaw to KEV on November 18.

severity.rationale: CISA confirms exploitation of a flaw reaching code execution in a credential-bearing AI proxy. The administrator credential prerequisite remains relevant.

affected.note: The reviewed database lists >=1.81.8,<1.83.10 and patched 1.83.10, while its patch instructions say 1.83.11.

exposure: Default configurations require a proxy-admin credential to reach POST /guardrails/test_custom_code. The default Docker image runs the proxy as root.

params.instructions: Check litellm version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Use 1.83.11 or later, following the more conservative patch instructions. If upgrading is delayed, block POST /guardrails/test_custom_code at the reverse proxy or gateway.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
